title: Singapore’s DayOne Pushes Ahead With Data Center IPO Tied to TikTok
source_used: The Information headline only (paywalled); context from The Business Times (15 Oct and 6 Oct 2026)
key_facts: The Information (16 Oct 2026) headline: Singapore's DayOne pushes ahead with a data center IPO tied to TikTok; the article text and the TikTok link could not be read.

Business Times, 15 Oct 2026: DayOne is among companies pushing ahead while other tech and data centre listings are delayed; AirTrunk is said to be delaying its Singapore REIT IPO until next year and Firmus's IPO was withdrawn in October.
DayOne filed for a US Nasdaq IPO in October, citing plans to raise as much as $5 billion; the Business Times put the potential valuation at about $20 billion.
DayOne's revenue more than tripled to $512 million in the first half of 2026, from $151.5 million a year earlier; it has raised over $6 billion in equity since 2024.
An analyst quoted by the Business Times noted the $20 billion valuation is roughly 20 times annualised sales of about $1 billion, with losses widening.
Business Times, 6 Oct 2026: DayOne develops and operates data centres for cloud and AI customers and began as a subsidiary of Shanghai-based GDS Holdings.
quote_evidence: Some are pushing ahead, however, like Singapore-headquartered data centre operator DayOne.
DayOne officially filed for a US Nasdaq IPO directly in October this year, citing plans to raise as much as US$5 billion.
DayOne's revenue more than tripled to US$512 million in the first half of this year, while raising over US$6 billion in equity since 2024
why_it_matters_hint: A loss-making data centre builder is going ahead with a multi-billion-dollar listing while peers delay theirs.
notes: The Information is paywalled (HTTP 200, no text). A 3-day and 14-day Google News search found no other outlet explaining the TikTok link, so it is left unexplained in the entry and attributed in quote marks. Context taken from the Business Times, read in full.
